title: The Staircase in the Scan — Postmortem CT, Photogrammetry & VR Stair-Fall Reconstruction (31/35 cm Injury Spacing vs. 32 cm Tread Depth), CPR Rib-Fracture CT vs. Autopsy Discordance & Ontario Fatal Stair Falls

teenKit.tldr: Forensic scientists use 3D digital scans, body measurements, and architectural blueprints to mathematically reconstruct how a person fell down a flight of stairs. By matching injury spacing to stair tread depth, they can separate tragic accidents from complex medical mysteries.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Bridging the gap between physical evidence and digital crime scenes helps investigators deliver absolute truth and justice when someone dies under ambiguous circumstances.
keyTakeaways: Researchers like Hariku Fukuda align postmortem CT scans and surface photogrammetry to map impact injuries in 3D space with millimeter precision.
The distance between specific marks on a body (like 31 cm and 35 cm intervals) can mirror the architectural dimensions of a staircase (like a 32 cm tread depth) to reconstruct a fall.
Medical scans and autopsies sometimes disagree—such as when detecting subtle rib fractures caused by life-saving CPR versus the actual trauma of an accident.

vocab.meaning: An advanced X-ray computed tomography scan performed on a body after death to map bones and internal injuries in 3D.
A technique that extracts precise 3D measurements and spatial relationships from overlapping photographs.
The horizontal flat surface of a stair that a person steps on when walking up or down.
A specialized branch of medicine focused on determining the cause of death by examining a corpse.

quiz.question: What was the significance of the numbers 31, 35, and 32 in the discussed case study?
options: They represented the victim's age, weight, and height.
They matched the inter-injury distances on the victim's body to the physical depth of a stair tread.
They were the coordinates of the room where the incident happened.
They tracked the exact time in seconds the fall lasted.
quiz.explanation: The measurements between impact marks on the body closely mirrored the 32 cm depth of the stairs where the victim was found.

quiz.question: What is the main purpose of combining photogrammetry and postmortem CT in forensic investigations?
options: To create a vivid virtual reality recreation of how a physical environment interacted with a body.
To replace human investigators with automated robots.
To clean up the physical crime scene faster.
To preserve the body indefinitely without refrigeration.
quiz.explanation: Integrating these technologies lets scientists bridge the physical and temporal gap between body injuries and the actual environment.

quiz.question: Why might postmortem CT scans and traditional autopsies sometimes show a discordance, such as with CPR rib fractures?
options: One of the methods is always completely inaccurate.
Different imaging and physical examination techniques reveal different structural details like buckle versus complete fractures.
Bones heal instantly after death, changing their appearance.
Medical examiners intentionally alter the data.
quiz.explanation: Scans and physical autopsies highlight different types of tissue and bone stress, which can lead to discrepancies in detecting subtle fractures.
